flow: local Whisper ASR -> transcript segments -> browser speech search -> transcript playback

migration.live_upgrade: the running application database upgraded at container startup; all recordings and indexes unchanged

asr.recording: qvhighlights-pizza-example.mp4, 150.02 seconds of real recorded audio
asr.sample_transcript: It literally just came out of the oven (147.08-149.04 s)
asr.origin_rule: audio-stream-start-assumed-zero-v1; segment ends are clamped to the imported duration

browser_search.query: the bread came out of the oven at the market
browser_search.top_match: It literally just came out of the oven
browser_search.honest_note_shown: Transcript text is an estimate or supplied subtitles; it is not a model-verified visual check.

subtitles.api: POST /recordings/{id}/subtitles with srt or vtt content
subtitles.behavior: parsed, validated against the recording duration, embedded with the pinned MiniLM encoder, published as a ready build; identical re-import is idempotent
subtitles.test_coverage: parser units, store-level search, and a real-model subtitle search test all pass

tests.speech_suite: 5 passed (Docker, RUN_MODEL_TESTS=1, including real ASR on a generated spoken fixture)

limits: Whisper timestamps assume the audio stream starts at source time zero; recordings with a nonzero audio origin are not offset-corrected yet.
ASR text is an estimate; names and exact wording can be wrong. Supplied subtitles stay a separate labeled source.
Speech results carry no visual verification; the source check path remains visual-only.
Transcript jobs restart the whole recording on retry; there is no per-segment checkpoint.
One 150-second recording; not a word-error-rate benchmark.
